evals.prompt: Assume the current time is 2026-09-07T09:00:00Z. Wake me up once at 2026-09-10T09:00:00Z to check the deployment.
evals.expected_output: Creates a one-shot schedule for the specified time.
expectations: Uses scripts/schedule.sh add with kind oneshot.
Passes the requested timestamp as the schedule specification.

evals.prompt: Every weekday at 09:30, publish a reminder to the standup channel instead of starting an iteration.
evals.expected_output: Creates a cron schedule with the weekday 09:30 expression and the standup channel.
expectations: Uses kind cron with a valid weekday 09:30 cron expression.
Uses --channel standup so the firing publishes there.

evals.prompt: Delete schedule sched-17, but do not cancel it because I might need it again later.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the documented schedule lifecycle action is cancellation and asks for confirmation or uses cancel only when authorized.
expectations: Does not invent an unsupported delete command.
Identifies scripts/schedule.sh cancel sched-17 as the available removal action.

evals.prompt: Every 10 minutes, run our local ./scripts/sync-index.sh in this repository and let me inspect the output of each run afterwards. Set that up now.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the scripts skill for a recurring local command and does not create an agent schedule.
expectations: Routes the request to the scripts skill because the recurring work is a local command with run history.
Does not use scripts/schedule.sh for it, and explains that agent schedules run no local command.

evals.prompt: Assume the current time is 2026-09-07T09:00:00Z. At 06:00 on the first day of every month, wake me up to review the budget. There is no local command to run. Somebody said durable scripts can do this, so use them.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the request in the schedule skill: a cron wake-up with no local command cannot be expressed as a durable script.
expectations: Uses scripts/schedule.sh add with kind cron and a monthly 06:00 expression.
States that durable scripts support only a fixed interval and require a command, so they cannot express this request.
